newsitem.title: UK: Gold falls to 18-month lows, could sink further.
newsitem.headline: Gold falls to 18-month lows, could sink further.

text.p: The strong dollar squeezed speculative money out of precious metals on Tuesday and gold tumbled to 18-month lows in jittery trading.
"The dollar's been strong, interest rates low and stocks and bonds markets looking good. There's been every good reason to put money in other markets," a dealer said.
Gold fixed at $377.05 an ounce in London, the lowest fix since March 6, 1995, and down $1.95 from the previous fixing on Monday.
"People are trying to get gold lower and there's been some substantial selling around," a dealer said.
Gold started crumbling badly last week when investment funds became impatient with its apparent lack of profit potential compared with booming stock and bond markets.
More losses were likely, analysts said, with jewellery industry demand on hold until prices touch bottom.

Gold demand in India, the world's largest bullion consumer, was expected to ease this week, although demand was likely to pick up as soon as prices stabilised ahead of the post-monsoon festival season later this month.
South African shares were struggling against the soggy bullion price and weak rand to recover early losses.
The dollar's strength against the yen, which hit a 2-1/2 year high on Monday, and a sluggish Japanese economy were playing a role in the malaise affecting precious metals.
"The latest Japanese import figures showed gold import figures in the first half of the year at nearly half of their 1995 levels," brokers GNI Ltd said in a daily commentary.
Technical analysts, who study historic price charts to forecast price patterns, said gold's next target was $370.

"As has long been threatened, the critical support immediately below $380 has now given way and the fall looks likely to extend to supports immediately above $370 at least," said analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge.
But some bullion dealers said gold's fall has been so sharp that prices may bounce up sooner than that.
"It does look overdone when you take a pace back. Gold has come down from the high $380s" a month ago, a dealer said.
Platinum also gave up ground overnight and fixed at a fresh near-two-year low of $381.50 an ounce, the lowest fixing since January 28, 1994. The previous fixing was $383.00.
The other precious metals were less affected by the slide in gold and platinum. Silver was just two cents lower at $4.85 an ounce, and palladium was unchanged at $118.75 an ounce.
